producer_report.summary:
`athena drain` now runs the independent items of one plan group at the same time, up to a new `[parallel] max_concurrency` setting. The default is 1, which is the old one-job-at-a-time drain. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` all pass.

**Root cause of the earlier failure.** The earlier attempt edited `athena.toml` without adding the schema field, so the config no longer parsed. Here the `[parallel]` section in `athena.toml` and the `Parallel` field in `crates/athena-data/src/config.rs` are in one change. The test `the_real_athena_toml_parses_with_its_parallel_section` parses the real `athena.toml` through `Config`.

**The `athena.toml` change.** The change is a new `[parallel]` section with `max_concurrency = 1`, placed at the end of the file. The value is 1 on purpose: the section adds the knob but changes no behaviour until the user raises it. The schema accepts 1 to 8; the ceiling is `MAX_CONCURRENCY_CEILING` in `config.rs`. The default and the ceiling are documented where they are defined, and in the `athena.toml` comment.

**The drain** (`crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs`):
- `drain()` keeps its signature and stays serial. The new `drain_concurrent(steps, limits, ui, max_concurrency)` is what `athena drain` calls, with the value read from the head commit's `athena.toml` (`main.rs`).
- Worker threads take items from a plan group. The next group starts only when the group before it is done, so a dependent item starts only after the item it needs has finished.
- Landing and rating are serialized by one lock.
- A model call's cap is held against the budget while the call is in flight, so jobs running side by side cannot overspend it. With bound 1 nothing is held across jobs.
- The first reason to stop wins. Once it is set, no worker starts another job, but jobs already started finish. Because it also stops siblings that have not yet started, a failed item at bound 2 or more can leave later items in the group unstarted.
- A worker panic is not isolated: the drain ends with that panic once the other workers finish. This is documented.

**Send + Sync changes (to disclose).**
- `jev::Evaluate` and `gh::HttpPost` now require `Send + Sync`, so the Athena handle can be shared between workers.
- The `ScriptedHttp` test double in `jev.rs` moved from `RefCell`/`Rc` to a mutex for the same reason.
- `RealSteps` now takes `Sync` UI and lander references. Existing call sites compiled unchanged.

**Tests:**
- In `crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs`, a `parallel` module covers five cases: bound 1 runs strictly in plan order; at bound 2 two independent items are in flight together (the barrier gives up after 5 s, so a serial drain fails with a peak of 1 rather than hanging); a dependent item starts after its dependency ends; a failure or a refusal leaves a sibling landing; the worker bound is never exceeded; a stop starts no further item; and in-flight caps stop a second job from overspending the budget.
- In `config.rs`: the real `athena.toml` parses, a config with no `[parallel]` gives 1, values 0 and 9 are rejected, and an unknown key inside `[parallel]` is rejected. The existing test already rejects an unknown top-level section.

**Docs.** The module and `Report` docs in `drain.rs`, the `plan.rs` module doc, the `athena drain --help` text in `main.rs`, `README.md` and `docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md` no longer say one job at a time. `docs/design/parallel-jobs.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` state what this slice built and what remains (multi-job `athena go`, the `--pr` phase). They also disclose the trait changes.

open_issues: `crates/athena-gate/src/content.rs` is not on the brief's deliverable list. I edited one test there (the `[parallel]` example became `[telemetry]`) because that test cannot pass otherwise. Please confirm that was allowed.
Scheduling is by plan group, so a later group in the same wave waits for earlier groups even if it would not conflict. Dependents are therefore conservative, not maximal.

Rating waits for the landing lock, so ratings can be queued behind landings. The budget-hold rule can also report `budget spent` slightly earlier at bound 2 or more than a serial run would, because in-flight caps count against the budget.
A worker panic is not isolated, as the brief allowed. It ends the drain after the other workers finish.
Parallel drain through `RealSteps` is only compile-checked: the new concurrency tests use a stub, because the fake-agent fixtures are single-job.
mistakes: The first build failed on two things: the `jev.rs` test double used `Rc<RefCell>`, and a comparison of the form `x as u32 < y` is parsed as generics. Both were fixed before finishing.
learnings: `Athena` was already Sync apart from `jev::Evaluate`, which holds `Box<dyn HttpPost>`. `Capability`, `Pinner` and `AgentDriver` were already `Send + Sync`, so only those two traits needed the bound.
`Plan::groups` flattened equals `Plan::order`, so scheduling by group keeps the existing order exactly.

Two existing tests used `[parallel]` as an example of an unknown section: `admission.rs` and `crates/athena-gate/src/content.rs`. Both break once the real file has `[parallel]` (a duplicate table), and neither is on the brief's deliverable list in the gate case.

The Bash hook allows only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm, and Grep and Read are limited to the working directory. The saved tool-result file for large output can't be read back, so use `cargo test -q`.
desires: A way to read saved tool output, or a quieter `cargo test` summary mode inside the allowed commands.
A fake-agent fixture that can run two jobs at once, to exercise `drain_concurrent` end to end through `RealSteps`.
